title: AutoPower: Automated Few-Shot Architecture-Level Power Modeling by Power Group Decoupling
problem: Traditional analytical architecture-level power models are inaccurate; recent ML-based approaches require sufficient training data from known configurations, which is unrealistic for early-stage power estimation with limited design configurations.
motivation: Power efficiency is critical in modern CPU design, but architects need fast and accurate power evaluation tools early in design to guide power optimization decisions.
method: AutoPower decouples power consumption into independent power groups (e.g., clock, SRAM, logic) and builds individual ML models for each group based on correlations with structural information available at the architecture level. Further decoupling within power groups creates multiple sub-models, enabling accurate few-shot learning with minimal training data.
key_novelty: Multi-level power group decoupling strategy enabling accurate architecture-level power modeling with only 2 known configurations, exploiting intrinsic structure of CPU power consumption.
contributions: Power group decoupling approach decomposing CPU power into independent components (clock, SRAM, logic)
Sub-model decomposition within each power group for finer-grained estimation
Few-shot ML-based power modeling requiring only 2 known configurations
4.36% mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) and 0.96 R^2 with 2 configurations; 5% lower MAPE than McPAT-Calib

metrics.other: MAPE: 4.36%; R^2: 0.96 with only 2 known configurations; 5% lower MAPE than McPAT-Calib, 0.09 higher R^2

limitations: Abstract does not discuss generalization across CPU architectures, impact of process technology variations, or comparison with other recent ML-based power modeling approaches.
primary_theme: Few-shot ML power model via power group decoupling
